patterns.title: Separate Reversible from Irreversible Decisions
patterns.short_description: Match deliberation to the cost of being wrong and the cost of changing course.
use_when: You are overanalyzing a low-cost choice or considering a commitment that may be hard to undo.
example_user_queries: I keep researching a choice I could easily undo.
How much thought does this decision deserve?
I'm about to make a commitment and want to know what could stick.
I can leave later, but switching would be expensive.
How do I decide which choices need more caution?
Can I try this before committing fully?
I want to know the downside if I change my mind.
I'm treating a major commitment like a harmless trial.

patterns.title: Define the Decision Before Comparing Options
patterns.short_description: Clarify the desired outcome and genuine constraints before judging alternatives.
use_when: You keep comparing options but suspect that the question itself is too narrow or unclear.
example_user_queries: I can't tell whether I need a new job or a different way of working.
I'm comparing two solutions but haven't defined the problem.
My choice feels like either staying forever or quitting immediately.
How do I find out what I really need from this decision?
I think some of these constraints might just be assumptions.
What alternatives am I missing?
We disagree about what we're actually deciding.
I want to improve the question before scoring the options.

patterns.title: Run a Premortem
patterns.short_description: Imagine a plan has failed, then identify plausible causes and safeguards before committing.
use_when: A favored plan has momentum and ordinary questions are not surfacing its vulnerabilities.
example_user_queries: Everyone likes this plan but I'm worried we're missing something.
What could realistically make this project fail?
I want to spot preventable risks before committing.
It's hard to criticize the plan once the team has agreed.
How do I turn a list of worries into changes to the plan?

Our project has several dependencies that could interact.

patterns.title: Prefer the Smallest Useful Experiment
patterns.short_description: Replace speculation with the smallest safe real-world test that teaches you something important.
use_when: Research cannot answer how a choice will work or feel in practice.
example_user_queries: I've researched this career but don't know whether I'd enjoy it.
How can I try self-employment without quitting my job?
I want to test whether people will actually pay.
What small action would tell me if this idea is feasible?
I keep working on the logo instead of testing demand.

patterns.title: Make Trade-offs Explicit
patterns.short_description: Name what each option gives you and what it asks you to sacrifice.
use_when: No option gives you everything, or repeated arguments conceal different priorities.
example_user_queries: I want a job with more money and freedom but can't find both.
How do I choose between a cheaper apartment and a shorter commute?

Which sacrifices am I actually willing to make?
My pros-and-cons list keeps getting longer.

patterns.title: Keep a Decision Journal
patterns.short_description: Record reasoning and expectations before outcomes make the past seem more predictable.
use_when: You want to learn from repeated, uncertain, or consequential decisions without confusing luck and judgment.
example_user_queries: I forget what I believed before I saw the result.

patterns.title: Map Outcomes, Likelihoods, and Preferences
patterns.short_description: Separate possible futures, their likelihood, and how much you value them.
use_when: Uncertain futures, hopes, and fears are getting mixed together while you compare options.
example_user_queries: I keep comparing job labels instead of the futures they could create.

patterns.short_description: Focus investigation on the uncertainty that could actually change what you choose.
